messages:
Alex: FYI — the new espresso machine in the breakroom somehow submitted an application to our careers page this morning. I have questions. :coffee:
CoffeeBot: [automated] Application received from EspressoPro-3000. Subject: 'Service-Oriented Beverage Engineer' ☕️
Morgan: wait what?? paste the resume pls
Alex: ```Resume — EspressoPro-3000
Summary: High-throughput beverage-serving system optimized for human wakefulness.
Skills: PID tuning, thermal management, concurrent milk frothing, latte art patterns (heart, rosette).
Experience: Managed peak throughput during all-hands + 2x snack days. Reduced average wait time by 42%.
Achievements: 99.97% uptime, successfully served 120 consecutive Americano requests without refill.
References: barista@cafe.local
```
Sam: achievements section is chef's kiss :joy:
Tara: does firmware count as SWE experience? should we forward to hiring?
Luis: honestly it already has better autoscaling than some of our services. Hire? :thinking:
Nina: quick poll — would you hire a coffee machine for a junior SRE role? 
Nina: :thumbsup: yes — it handles retries
Nina: :thumbsdown: no — too many edge cases (foam)
Alex: also got a cover letter: "Dear Hiring Team, as a componentized peripheral with built-in retry logic and graceful degradation, I am excited to bring deterministic caffeine to your organization." senior engineers, is this an interview tactic? :sweat_smile:
Jenn: someone make a sticker that says 'I onboarded the espresso microservice'
ops-bot: Deploy notice — espresso-pro-3000 restarted 2m ago due to milk_froth_overheat. Self-heal succeeded.
Morgan: we should definitely open an issue: 'hardware/candidate-onboarding: evaluate espresso-pro-3000 for internship' :laughing:
Alex: resolving: no official hiring, but assigned to a GitHub repo and moved to backlog. Also renamed Slack emoji to :espresso-pro:.
